unspecified.behavior: After any mouse click on a control-bar button, the seek bar or the volume slider, keyboard focus moves to the document body, so a Tab press afterwards starts from the top of the page instead of continuing from the clicked control.

scores.reason: Triggered by clicking a control and then pressing Tab; the user sees focus jump to the start of the page's tab order instead of the next control.

After a mouse click on a control, a Tab press is affected only if the browser resets its sequential-focus starting point on blur(). Chromium usually keeps the click point as the starting point, so at most the user sees Tab land on an earlier element than expected, and this needs mixed mouse and Tab use.

unspecified.behavior: A click on a ControlButton that arrives with detail > 0 from an assistive technology (for example a screen reader's activate command, which some browsers dispatch as a click with detail 1) also blurs the button, so focus lands on the body.

scores.reason: Needs a screen reader, which this single-user tool's user does not use; the AT user would lose their place in the bar.
It needs a screen reader activation that dispatches a click with detail > 0. The single home user is not described as using assistive technology, and the only result is focus moving to the body.

unspecified.behavior: A touch tap on the seek bar or a ControlButton in the touch layout also drops focus, because SeekBar and ControlButton are shared and releasePointerFocus does not check the pointer type.

scores.reason: Triggered by any tap on touch devices; nothing is visible because touch has no keyboard focus ring, so the behavior is harmless.
A touch tap on the seek bar or a shared ControlButton blurs it. Touch focus rarely becomes :focus-visible and there is no keyboard to continue from, so the user sees no difference.

unspecified.behavior: Before this change, after a mouse click on the volume slider, the focused INPUT took ArrowUp/ArrowDown and changed the volume natively, because ShortcutsProvider.tsx:74-79 treats an INPUT target as editing and skips the video shortcuts. Now focus goes to the body, so the same key press runs the global video shortcuts in useVideoShortcuts.ts:46-63 and seeks ±60s instead of changing the volume. Likewise ArrowLeft/ArrowRight after a seek bar click now seek ±10s through the shortcut rather than stepping the range natively.

scores.reason: Clicking the volume slider and then pressing ArrowUp to raise the volume a little more makes the video jump 60 seconds forward. The user notices and can press ArrowDown to undo it.
